      "text": "\n\n\nBecause a \"Live USB\" is essentially a bootable operating system, it creates multiple hidden partitions on your flash drive (which is why it is currently showing up as two separate drives, D: and E:). \n\nSimply right-clicking them in \"My Computer\" and hitting \"Format\" won\u0027t work properly, as it will only format one of the partitions and leave you with missing storage space. \n\nTo completely wipe the USB and merge it back into a single usable drive, the most reliable way on Windows is to use the built-in **Diskpart** tool. \n\n***⚠️ CRITICAL WARNING:*** *This process will permanently erase everything on the drive you select. Please unplug any other external hard drives or USBs so you don\u0027t accidentally erase the wrong one.*\n\n### The Most Reliable Method: Using Diskpart\n\n1. **Open Command Prompt as Administrator:**\n   * Press the **Windows Key**, type **`cmd`**.\n   * Right-click on **Command Prompt** and select **Run as administrator**.\n\n2. **Start Diskpart:**\n   * In the black window, type **`diskpart`** and press **Enter**.\n\n3. **Find your USB Drive:**\n   * Type **`list disk`** and press **Enter**.\n   * You will see a list of disks (Disk 0, Disk 1, Disk 2, etc.). Look at the **Size** column to identify your USB drive. (For example, a 32GB flash drive will usually show up as roughly 28 GB or 29 GB).\n\n4. **Select your USB Drive:**\n   * Type **`select disk X`** (replace **X** with the number of your USB drive from the previous step) and press **Enter**. \n   * *Make absolutely sure you have the right number!*\n\n5. **Wipe the drive:**\n   * Type **`clean`** and press **Enter**. (This instantly wipes all partitions, merging D: and E: back into raw, unallocated space).\n\n6. **Create a new partition:**\n   * Type **`create partition primary`** and press **Enter**.\n\n7. **Format the drive:**\n   * Type **`format fs\u003dexfat quick`** and press **Enter**. \n   * *(Note: We use `exfat` because it allows you to store files larger than 4GB and works perfectly on both Windows and Mac. If you only use Windows, you can type `format fs\u003dntfs quick` instead).*\n\n8. **Assign a drive letter:**\n   * Type **`assign`** and press **Enter**. This will automatically mount the drive back into Windows under a single, new letter.\n\n9. **Exit:**\n   * Type **`exit`** and press Enter to close Diskpart.\n\nYour USB drive is now completely factory-reset into a single partition and ready to be used for normal file storage!",
      "role": "model",

      "text": "\n\n\nAh, I see the issue. You ran into the **\"There is no media in the device\"** error. \n\nBased on your screenshots, this usually happens for one of two reasons:\n\n**1.
